title: Open-geocoder integration + dedup/reconciliation with precedence + confidence flagging
context: Geocoding errors can place a food-assistance entry at the wrong location, sending a food-insecure person to the wrong address — real harm. Only open geocoders whose terms permit storing results are permitted (OSM/Nominatim, Pelias, US Census Geocoder). Low-confidence geocodes must be flagged for human review rather than published silently. Deduplication must preserve the full source trail so closures and corrections are never lost. Depends on food-maps-ingest-007 (adapters producing staging entries).
objective: Implement the geocoding and deduplication stages of the pipeline: (1) a geocoding module that resolves addresses using an open geocoder (Nominatim, Pelias, or US Census Geocoder), records geocode_source, confidence level, and the resolved coordinates per entry, and flags low-confidence results for human review rather than publishing them; (2) a deduplication/reconciliation module that clusters likely-duplicate entries across sources, merges them using a precedence rule (authoritative/operator source wins), and preserves the full source trail in sources[].
acceptanceCriteria: Geocoding uses only open geocoders whose terms permit storing results (Nominatim, Pelias, or US Census Geocoder); no proprietary geocoder whose terms forbid stored results
Each geocoded entry records geocode_source (which geocoder) and a confidence level (high/medium/low)
Low-confidence geocodes are flagged in the entry's metadata and excluded from the authoritative published set until a human confirms them
Entries with a geocoding mismatch vs. the source address are flagged for review
Deduplication clusters entries that represent the same physical location/service across sources using deterministic matching (address normalization + name similarity or spatial proximity)
Merged entries preserve the full sources[] trail from all contributing source records (no provenance is dropped on merge)
Precedence rule is documented and applied: authoritative/operator-published source wins over aggregated sources for conflicting facts
Closure signals from any source demote the merged entry's operating_status and are never lost on merge

Unit tests cover: a high-confidence geocode passes; a low-confidence geocode is flagged; two records for the same location from different sources merge with both sources preserved; a closure from one source propagates to the merged entry
output: src/pipeline/geocode.ts + src/pipeline/dedup.ts with unit tests, integrated into the pipeline core and passing CI.
